scope: The eight src/apps/* CLI front-ends named as next by M34. Contract checks against OpenSSL 3.6.4 for argument-string lifetimes, option-table bounds, file/BIO ownership on every exit, error tails, getter-returned raw pointers and allocation arithmetic; genuine cleanup, option-routing and arithmetic defects repaired.
worktree: source: src/apps/{enc,kdf}.rs repaired; src/apps/{ecparam,ec,engine,errstr,genrsa,info}.rs audited with no source change. queue/receipt: REMAINING-AUDIT.txt, AUDITED-FILES.txt, PERFILE-INDEX.md section 39 and this file.

file_dispositions.note: EC_get_builtin_curves returns the table count and writes min(nitems,count); both calls use the count as nitems, so the single set_len(filled) assertion is exact. The four-slot parameter array holds at most three entries plus the end terminator. Every params_key/out/key/pctx/ectx exit releases once; EVP_PKEY_keygen writes only on success. OSSL_ENCODER_to_bio accepts a NULL context (returns the authority's encoder-not-found failure), so the omitted explicit null check matches observable behaviour. -no_seed and -check_named reach not_landed rather than fabricating the unlanded arms.

mechanisms: bio_open_default output BIO on every exit
file_dispositions.note: Each CString lives across its parameter call; eckey and out are released exactly once on every path (including all setter, print and check failures). The encoder path passes OPT_FMT_PEMDER selection as the authority does. Retained shared divergence: bio_open_owner's owner-only permissions are not reconstructed (private is computed but unused); OSSL_ENCODER_to_bio tolerates NULL and reports the same 'unable to write EC key'.

mechanisms: BIO chain ownership for base64/cipher push
file_dispositions.note: The header documents the EVP_SKEY/EVP_SKEYMGMT path as not landed, but -skeyopt only set a flag and -skeymgmt was stored and ignored. With a cipher and no -K, the body then continued into the raw-key path and initialised the cipher with the all-zero key buffer, and -skeyopt/-K was silently accepted where the authority refuses the combination. Both options now return not_landed at parse time. set_hex indexes out[i/2] only for i < 2*out.len(); bsize reproduces the authority's k/opt_long/LONG_MAX/1024 check; the cleanup order (BIO_free(in), BIO_free_all(out), BIO_free(benc), BIO_free(b64), EVP_CIPHER_free) matches apps/enc.c:801-821 and never dereferences a freed chain link.

mechanisms: ENGINE_by_id functional reference vs ENGINE_get_first/get_next structural pointer
BIO owners for stdout/stderr and every early exit
file_dispositions.note: Only ENGINE_by_id answers a functional reference, and only that pointer is ENGINE_free'd; the listing walk uses the structural pointer the authority does not free. Engine id/name getters are NULL-checked before CStr. cname/carg CStrings outlive ENGINE_ctrl_cmd_string. out is freed on every parse refusal and at end; the per-failure stderr BIO is freed immediately. No new boundary.

ERR_error_string_n is given the exact buffer length and the buffer is NUL-terminated; the CStr borrow is scoped before the buffer goes out of scope. OPENSSL_init_ssl's settings argument is NULL and documented. parse_hex_l performs wrapping arithmetic only and cannot index past the input. The documented GNU/POSIX strerror divergence is unchanged.

mechanisms: BN_new/BN_GENCB_new single-owner release on every exit
strtol base-0 conversion and opt_int range check
file_dispositions.note: Every path after the two allocations frees both exactly once; NULL is accepted by BN_free/BN_GENCB_free. Numeric conversion rejects trailing characters, empty subjects, and positive overflow. Negative magnitudes beyond LONG_MAX+1 are accepted as LONG_MIN and then rejected by opt_int as outside integer range (authority rejects with 'Can't parse ... as a number'); both exit 1, message differs. Generation remains not_landed as documented.
The single raw getter is NULL-checked before CStr, and the returned pointer is documented as a 'static NUL-terminated string. dirty/type accounting has no indexing. No change.

mechanisms: app_params_new_from_opts OSSL_PARAM array allocation and free
file_dispositions.note: The OSSL_PARAM array was allocated as (opts.len()+1) * size_of::<OSSL_PARAM>() without checked arithmetic, although the authority's OPENSSL_calloc rejects an overflowing product. It now uses checked_add/checked_mul and answers NULL (the call's existing malformed-option failure) on overflow. The terminator is written at index sz within the allocated entry count. Every exit releases params, out, ctx, kdf, dkm_bytes and hexout once; dkm_bytes is the cleansed owned block and hexout the plain-adopt block.

defects.description: The module header says -skeyopt/-skeymgmt reach not_landed, but -skeyopt only set a flag and -skeymgmt was stored and ignored. With a cipher and no -K, parsing then fell through to the raw-key path and called EVP_CipherInit_ex with the all-zero key buffer; -skeyopt together with -K was silently accepted instead of the authority's 'Either a raw key or the skeyopt args' refusal.
defects.repair: Both option arms now return not_landed at parse time, so the opaque-key path cannot silently degrade to a zero key. No unsafe operation changed.

defects.description: app_params_new_from_opts sized the params array with (opts.len() + 1) * size_of::<OSSL_PARAM>() without checked arithmetic. A wrapping product would under-allocate a block later written through params.add(i)/params.add(sz). The input is argv-derived and unreachable at present lengths, but the authority's OPENSSL_calloc rejects the overflow and §3 requires the check.
defects.repair: checked_add(1) and checked_mul(size_of) with a NULL return (the function's existing failure value).

unsafe_operations_note: Neither repair adds or removes an unsafe expression: the enc fix is control flow at two safe option arms, and the kdf fix replaces a wrapping multiplication inside an existing safe allocation expression. No new FFI symbol, allocator coordinate, #[repr(C)] layout or signature.
